findings.claim: The exclusivity claim carrying this row's unit_type warrant ('a two-token sung-imperative pair unique book-wide at every tier' / 'its only sung-imperative pair') ships without the mandated adjacent digit-bearing sweep citation, and the same device_notes sentence attributes the MT splice to a web: ref.
findings.grounds: The claim is byte-true on re-sweep: פִּצְח֤וּ רַנְּנוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.52.9, byte tier) stands at 1 verse at byte tier, 1 at accent_stripped and 1 at skeleton (sweep: 1 verse at each of the three tiers), so the correct digit is available and simply absent from both the boundary_rationale and device_notes statements. Separately, device_notes reads 'spliced at byte tier at web:Isa.52.9' while the boundary_rationale cites the same splice correctly as oshb:Isa.52.9; the pointed text is MT-keyed and belongs under the oshb: prefix.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: append the sanctioned shorthand (sweep: 1 verse at every tier) to the uniqueness claim in boundary_rationale and device_notes, and change 'spliced at byte tier at web:Isa.52.9' to the oshb: form already used in the rationale.

findings.claim: 'A further SAMEKH mark (single-witness) sits at this span's own close' opens with a comparative that has no antecedent inside this row; its antecedent lives in a neighbouring row's prose.
findings.grounds: This row cites exactly one parashah mark, at oshb:Isa.52.10 (SAMEKH, single-witness, verified against the MT-keyed inventory), and mentions no earlier mark anywhere in any field, so 'a further' is an orphaned cross-row comparative rather than a verse-anchored reference. The neighbouring rows that do carry an in-row antecedent use the same wording legitimately, which is what makes this instance a leak rather than a style choice.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: drop 'further' ('A SAMEKH mark (single-witness) sits at this span's own close, oshb:Isa.52.10').

findings.claim: The hearing-echo digit is bound to the wrong count object: the row names a three-letter consonantal-root tier and cites 'sweep: 30 verses book-wide', but the three-letter root sweeps to 84 verses; 30 is the count for a four-letter string that does not occur in one of the two cited sites, so no sweep in the row backs the echo it is offered for.
findings.grounds: Re-swept over the MT text with the count object named each time: the three-letter consonantal root shared by שָׁמְע֖וּ (oshb:Isa.52.15, byte tier) and לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte tier) stands as a contiguous consonantal substring in 84 verses (sweep: 84 verses), as a whole word-bound token in 10 verses (sweep: 10 verses), and token-initially in 51 verses (sweep: 51 verses). The cited digit 30 is the substring count for the four-letter form of שָׁמְע֖וּ (sweep: 30 verses); that four-letter string is absent from the consonantal skeleton of לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ, so the 30-verse object cannot contain the second site of the claimed echo at all.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: replace '(sweep: 30 verses book-wide)' with the three-letter root's own digit and unit (sweep: 84 verses book-wide, contiguous consonantal substring), or re-name the count object to the form the 30 actually counts.

findings.claim: The arm-noun echo is asserted first at word-bound skeleton tier, but the 53:1 member of the pair is absent from the three-verse word-bound list the same sentence cites; the link holds only at the prefix-tolerant tier named second.
findings.grounds: Re-swept with both count objects named: the bare form זְר֣וֹעַ (oshb:Isa.52.10, byte tier) is word-bound at skeleton tier in exactly 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses -- oshb:Isa.51.9, oshb:Isa.52.10, oshb:Isa.63.12), which the row cites correctly and which does not include oshb:Isa.53.1; the prefixed form וּזְר֥וֹעַ (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte tier) enters only under the prefix-tolerant object, at 6 verses (sweep: 6 verses, adding oshb:Isa.44.12, oshb:Isa.53.1, oshb:Isa.62.8), also cited correctly. Both digits re-derive exactly; what is wrong is the order of assertion, which links the two sites at a tier whose own cited list excludes one of them. Read to the end of the sentence the disclosure is present, which is why this is graded low.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: state the link at the prefix-tolerant tier first and keep the word-bound 3-verse sweep as the narrower object it is.

findings.claim: The rear seam is driven by a person-shift while a person-shift of another kind stands inside the span two verses earlier and is declined as a seam, and the discriminating principle (speaker change versus addressee change) is implied but never stated as the rule.
findings.grounds: The row's own bytes carry the internal shift it declines, עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Isa.52.14, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse at byte tier) giving way to עָלָ֛יו (oshb:Isa.52.15, byte tier), and its rear-seam driver, לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse at every tier). The row's own strongest_rejected_alternative concedes that no frame-formula onset marks the rear seam, so the person-shift is the whole warrant there; the campaign standard applied at the neighbouring seam is that a clause-type already standing inside a row does not discriminate the seam it is offered for.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: name the discriminator explicitly (a change of speaking voice at the rear seam versus a change of addressee inside the span) rather than describing both as person-shifts.

findings.claim: The parashah characterization is contradicted by the inventory the row itself cites: three of the four setumah sites fall precisely on this row's own named signature closings, which are also three of the four cut points of the rival the row rejects, so the layer corroborates the finer reading rather than 'a longer reading over a finer one'.
findings.grounds: The MT-keyed single-witness inventory carries SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.53.12, oshb:Isa.54.8, oshb:Isa.54.10 and oshb:Isa.54.17 and at no other verse in oshb:Isa.54.1-Isa.54.17 -- the row's four cited sites re-derive exactly. But oshb:Isa.54.8 closes on אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.8, byte tier), oshb:Isa.54.10 closes on אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.10, byte tier) and oshb:Isa.54.17 closes on נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.54.17, byte tier) -- the very signature closings the row's strongest_rejected_alternative offers as the rival's cut points, alongside oshb:Isa.54.6. The interval oshb:Isa.54.8 to oshb:Isa.54.10 is two verses, so 'wide intervals rather than at the signature closings individually' is false on its own cited data. The finding is graded medium and not high because this layer is tier-3 weak corroboration that is never a driver, and the row's actual seam driver is the byte-grounded feminine-singular vocative onset at oshb:Isa.54.1.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: state that the mark sites coincide with three of the four rival cut points and that the layer therefore supplies no tier-3 corroboration for the longer reading, dropping the 'wide intervals' and 'corroborating a longer reading over a finer one' clauses.

findings.claim: 'the prefixed form heading web:Isa.55.5' is byte-false: the prefixed title stands as the fourteenth of that verse's seventeen tokens, and the verse is headed by a different word.
findings.grounds: oshb:Isa.55.5 opens on הֵ֣ן (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier); the prefixed title וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier) occupies token positions 14-15 of 17 in the source bytes. The underlying tier claim is sound -- קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.54.5, byte tier) is not a byte substring of oshb:Isa.55.5 and is a substring only once cantillation is stripped -- so the defect is confined to the position word, which is not load-bearing for the seam.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: replace 'heading web:Isa.55.5' with 'standing inside web:Isa.55.5' (or a neutral 'at web:Isa.55.5').

findings.claim: device_notes carries campaign-governance narration in row prose: the confidence sentence describes 'the medium_low ceiling the campaign holds for whole-chapter units' and 'a level implying a fresh defect'.
findings.grounds: The register rule bars workflow and review-process language in every row field; the substantive fact -- that this span covers all seventeen verses of its chapter -- is already stated in the same sentence and carries the confidence band on its own without narrating the campaign's rule or the review's defect-finding.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: reduce to the substantive statement (this span covers all seventeen verses of its chapter, and its confidence is held at medium_low), dropping the campaign-rule and defect-narration clauses.

findings.claim: The rear-seam driver is corroborated by a claim about translation behaviour -- 'a turn neither witness's English marks, since both render every surrounding pronoun the same way' -- which is tier-4 metadata used as corroboration and which presupposes a second English witness that the staged corpus does not carry.
findings.grounds: The Hebrew fact the sentence supports is byte-checkable and correct on its own: oshb:Isa.55.5 runs masculine singular throughout, from תֵדַע֙ through אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ and פֵאֲרָֽךְ (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier), and it is the only one of the seven verses oshb:Isa.55.1-Isa.55.7 that carries a singular-you suffix -- oshb:Isa.55.3 runs masculine plural at אָזְנְכֶם֙ and נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.55.3, byte tier), oshb:Isa.55.2 likewise closes plural at נַפְשְׁכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.55.2, byte tier), and oshb:Isa.55.1, oshb:Isa.55.4, oshb:Isa.55.6 and oshb:Isa.55.7 carry no second-person suffix at all. What fails is the corroboration attached to it: how a translation renders a pronoun is tier-4 metadata and is never boundary evidence or corroboration, and 'neither witness's English' plus 'both render' asserts a comparison across two English witnesses when the staged corpus carries exactly one English witness against the MT.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: delete the translation-rendering clause and let the singular-turn stand on the pointed bytes and the seven-verse suffix sweep already in the field.

findings.claim: The stated cause of the tier degradation is wrong: 'the prefix attached here changes the leading bytes, so the two meet where cantillation is stripped away' -- stripping cantillation does not remove a prefix, and the count object (unbound substring rather than word-bound) is never named.
findings.grounds: וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.55.5, byte tier) and קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.54.5, byte tier) differ in two independent ways: the accents differ, which is what defeats byte tier, and the prefix breaks the word bound, which it does at every tier including the accent-stripped one. They meet only as an unbound accent-stripped substring; the pointed title form at oshb:Isa.54.5 stands at 3 verses at byte tier (sweep: 3 verses) and its accent-stripped substring at 17 verses (sweep: 17 verses, oshb:Isa.55.5 among them). The tier label the row assigns is correct; the causal explanation and the missing count object are not.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: say that the accents defeat byte tier while the prefix breaks the word bound, and name the object as an accent-stripped substring match with its digit.

findings.claim: The addressee-number driver yields two candidate seam positions and the row discloses neither the rival nor a discriminator: if the shift of addressee number is the warrant, the plural-to-singular turn at the front of oshb:Isa.55.5 is as much a seam as the singular-to-plural return at oshb:Isa.55.6, and the row's stated rival is a different one entirely.
findings.grounds: The bytes give a plural addressee through oshb:Isa.55.3, no second person at all in oshb:Isa.55.4, a wholly masculine-singular oshb:Isa.55.5, and a return to plural imperatives at דִּרְשׁ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.55.6, byte tier). A verse-initial plural imperative does not discriminate the chosen position either: הַטּ֤וּ (oshb:Isa.55.3, byte tier) is also verse-initial and לְכ֣וּ (oshb:Isa.55.1, byte tier) stands inside the preceding span, which the row itself concedes when it says the form-class is unchanged. The only remaining discriminator between a cut before oshb:Isa.55.5 and a cut before oshb:Isa.55.6 is the tier-3 SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.55.5, which is weak corroboration in the Prophets and never a driver. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative instead answers an undivided-chapter reading, leaving the nearer rival unaddressed.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: disclose the cut-before-oshb:Isa.55.5 rival as the strongest one and name the byte-grounded discriminator that keeps the singular verse with the invitation rather than with the summons.

findings.claim: The signal key speech_formula.imperative_onset mis-names the class of the signal it records; the device is an imperative onset, not a speech formula, and the identical signal is keyed oracle_frame.imperative_onset by the rows on either side in book order.
findings.grounds: The device the key stands for is דִּרְשׁ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.55.6, byte tier), a verse-initial imperative, which is an oracle-frame onset signal; the row's other two keys are correctly assigned, the postpositive signature covering נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה at oshb:Isa.55.8 and the frame-architecture key covering the preserved seam at web:Isa.55.13 to web:Isa.56.1.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: re-key speech_formula.imperative_onset to oracle_frame.imperative_onset.

findings.claim: The same byte construction is load-bearing in opposite directions inside this batch without a stated principle: a verse-initial conjunction plus messenger formula is argued here as a reason NOT to cut at web:Isa.56.3 to web:Isa.56.4, while the identical construction is the seam driver at web:Isa.52.3 to web:Isa.52.4 in the rows that ship the preceding spans.
findings.grounds: This row's own device_notes reasons from the subordination -- the frame כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.56.4, byte tier) is preceded by כִּי (oshb:Isa.56.4, byte tier), so the formula is not verse-initial. That is byte-true, and it is equally byte-true of כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ (oshb:Isa.52.4, byte tier) against כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר (oshb:Isa.52.3, byte tier), where the same construction is treated as a fresh frame onset opening a new unit. The construction is one object book-wide: it stands at 14 verses at consonantal-skeleton tier (sweep: 14 verses, word-bound and substring counts agreeing), oshb:Isa.52.3, oshb:Isa.52.4 and oshb:Isa.56.4 among them, and all three sit on the divine side of the koh-amar census. No field in either row names a discriminator, so the warrant column is incoherent across the batch. Recorded, not adjudicated: both seams rest on a ruled tier-1 frame onset standing in their own bytes, so no respan is proposed here.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: state the discriminating principle that lets a verse-initial conjunction plus messenger formula reinforce an ongoing frame here while opening a fresh one at web:Isa.52.4 -- or route the pair for a single adjudicated ruling.

findings.claim: Every parashah and paseq claim in boundary_evidence_refs is cited under a web: prefix, and the device_notes setumah claims under bare refs, although the seg layer is MT-keyed to a single MT witness; the row contradicts itself by citing the same paseq correctly as oshb:Isa.56.4 in device_notes.
findings.grounds: The mark inventory declares MT numbering and a single MT witness on its face, and every other row in this batch cites marks under the oshb: prefix. Here boundary_evidence_refs carries 'web:Isa.55.13 (setumah, single-witness)', 'web:Isa.56.2 (setumah, single-witness)', 'web:Isa.56.3 (setumah, single-witness)', 'web:Isa.56.5 (setumah, single-witness)' and 'web:Isa.56.4 (paseq, single-witness)', while device_notes writes 'oshb:Isa.56.4 carries a single paseq seg' for the same object. The claims themselves re-derive correctly against the inventory at MT keys -- SAMEKH at 55:13, 56:2, 56:3 and 56:5 with the petuchah type never invoked, and a single paseq seg at 56:4 with no intra-verse position claimed -- so the defect is the witness and numbering-space attribution, not the content. It is arithmetically inert only because these chapters are identity chapters; the same habit in either offset zone would be a coordinate error.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: re-prefix all five mark entries in boundary_evidence_refs, and the four bare device_notes mark refs, to oshb:.

findings.claim: 'the formula class is postpositive elsewhere across the book's koh-amar/neum census' is an exclusivity claim carrying no adjacent digit-bearing sweep, though it re-derives as true and could carry a strong digit.
findings.grounds: Re-swept with the object named: the postpositive signature stands in 23 verses book-wide (sweep: 23 verses), and this row's site is the only one of them where the formula is the verse's first token (sweep: 1 verse) -- נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Isa.56.8, byte tier). The universal is byte-true; only the mandated digit is missing.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: add the digit, e.g. the sole verse-initial site of a 23-verse postpositive census (sweep: 23 verses; 1 verse-initial).

findings.claim: 'stands verse-initial and heads the gathering clause it introduces' overstates the Hebrew: the formula is verse-initial, but an appositional epithet and the verse's main pause stand between it and the clause the English quotation gives.
findings.grounds: נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Isa.56.8, byte tier) is followed immediately by מְקַבֵּ֖ץ נִדְחֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.56.8, byte tier), an epithet in apposition to the divine name, and only then, after the atnach, by ע֛וֹד אֲקַבֵּ֥ץ עָלָ֖יו לְנִקְבָּצָֽיו (oshb:Isa.56.8, byte tier), the clause the row quotes in English. The load-bearing half of the sentence -- that this instance is not a postpositive seal, so the row does not close at web:Isa.56.8 on a closing formula -- survives the correction untouched, which is why this is graded low; the ordering the sentence describes matches the WEB sentence's placement of 'says' rather than the Hebrew word order.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: say the formula stands verse-initial and heads the verse, with the gathering clause following its appositional epithet.
